title: Nebula Retail — Token cost scenarios and Redwood Optimize recommendations
content:
Executive summary:

This sheet summarizes a before/after cost model for Nebula Retail (chat+generation product line) and a prioritized set of Redwood Optimize levers. Baseline hosted costs are estimated at $36k/month for current traffic patterns (1.8B tokens/month). Our recommended combination of model tiering, int4 quantization, prefix KV caching, smarter batching, and a modest reserved commit reduces run-rate to ~ $11.2k/month — ~69% recurring savings. One-time engineering and migration effort is estimated at 160–220 hours (3–5 weeks of mixed effort).

Key assumptions (customer-provided + validated):
- Traffic: 18M requests/month; average response size = 100 tokens => 1.8B generated tokens/month.
- Baseline model: open-llama-30b-fp16 hosted endpoint; list rate used for baseline calc = $0.020 per 1k tokens.
- No existing prefix/KV caching in prod; request duplication (repeated prompts / system prompts) estimated at 12% of tokens.
- 65% of sessions are low-risk for model regression (factual strictness not required), suitable for smaller 13B tuned variant.
- Target SLO: p95 latency < 600ms (user-facing), error/free-run quality acceptable for pilot.

Baseline (Before Redwood Optimize):
- Monthly tokens: 1.8B (1,800,000k)
- Baseline unit rate: $0.020 / 1k tokens
- Monthly cost = 1,800,000 * $0.020 = $36,000
- Observed pain points: token spend variability, occasional latency spikes during peak hour, limited visibility into token-level cost by route.

Redwood Optimize recommended configuration (summary):
1) Model tiering: route 65% of sessions to a tuned 13B quantizable variant for answer types that tolerate smaller context/model capacity.
2) Quantization: deploy int4 (4-bit) quantized variant for both 13B and 30B where validation shows parity on our eval suite — yields ~40% per-inference compute reduction over fp16 for same model family.
3) Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix caching on 12% of token volume (repeated system/prompt prefixes) to reduce effective tokens processed.
4) Batching + autoscaling policy tuning: increase continuous batching window by 8ms and configure workload-aware batch sizes to improve GPU utilization without exceeding p95 SLOs (estimated 8% effective cost reduction for serving).
5) Reserved Dedicated commit (optional): negotiate a 3–6 month reserved capacity commit for predictable peak capacity to net further ~10% unit cost discount on managed-hosting line items.

Blended post-optimize math (stepwise):
- Step A: After model-tiering + quantization blended per-1k rate:
  - quantized 13B rate (expected) = $0.006 / 1k tokens
  - quantized 30B rate (expected) = $0.012 / 1k tokens
  - 65% @ 13B, 35% @ 30B => blended rate = 0.65*0.006 + 0.35*0.012 = $0.0081 / 1k tokens
- Step B: Apply prefix-caching (12% reduction in effective processed tokens):
  - effective tokens = 1.8B * (1 - 0.12) = 1.584B => 1,584,000k tokens
- Step C: Apply batching/ops improvements (estimated 8% direct savings) and reserved-commit negotiation (further 5% conservative estimate if pursued); combined conservative ops discount assumed for model = 13% total (0.13) on the blended spend.
- Final monthly cost = 1,584,000k * $0.0081 * (1 - 0.13) ≈ $11,167/month

Savings summary: 
- Baseline: $36,000/month
- Post-optimize recurring: ~$11,167/month
- Gross monthly savings: ~$24,833 (~69% reduction)
- Annualized run-rate savings: ~$298k/year (excl. reserved commit one-time discounts and negotiation).

One-time and non-recurring costs: 
- Engineering migration and validation: 160–220h (3–5 weeks) across infra + platform + MLE (estimated internal cost: equivalent to $18k–$28k fully-burdened).
- Validation & eval suites: ~40–80h to run curated prompts and holdback tests (quality/regression monitoring).
- Total non-recurring: budget recommendation = $25k contingent for pilot.

Sensitivity scenarios (quick):
- Low caching realization (only 6% instead of 12%): final cost ≈ $12.8k/mo => 64% savings vs baseline.
- Lower tiering adoption (50% to 13B, 50% to 30B): blended rate = 0.5*0.006 + 0.5*0.012 = 0.009 => final cost ≈ $12.4k/mo => 65% savings.
- 20% traffic growth without mitigation: baseline cost would be $43.2k -> post-optimize grows proportionally (~$13.4k) but still ~69% savings relative to that new baseline.

Quality & risk matrix (high level):
- Regression risk: moderate for switching 65% of sessions to 13B; mitigations: A/B canary, evaluate on named prompt sets, auto rollback based on eval metrics and retention of some traffic to 30B variant.
- Latency risk: small — quantized models typically improve latency; monitor p95 and p99 closely.
- Operational complexity: low–medium: requires deployment of quantized variants, KV caching config, and routing policy; Redwood Console supports rollout and tracing.

Recommended next steps (prioritized):
1) Run a 4-week pilot (canary) covering 5% -> 20% -> 50% traffic to 13B quantized variant with mirrored eval logging.
2) Enable prefix/KV caching in staging and measure realized token reduction on a 2-week dataset cut.
3) Implement batching/auto-tune policy in pre-prod and baseline end-to-end latency impact.
4) Prepare reserved-capacity negotiation if pilot shows >50% stable adoption; Redwood sales to propose a 6-month commit term with staged ramp.
5) Create an eval dashboard with prompt-level quality checks and cost per-route reporting (owner: Nebula infra + Redwood solutions-eng).

Appendix — quick spreadsheet table (flattened):
- Rows: metric, baseline, post-opt:
  - monthly_tokens_k: 1800000, 1584000
  - blended_rate_per_1k: $0.020, $0.0081
  - ops_discount: 0%, 13%
  - monthly_cost: $36,000, $11,167
  - monthly_savings_abs: -, $24,833
  - monthly_savings_pct: -, 69%

Notes and open questions for Nebula team:
- Confirm fraction of sessions requiring high-capacity model: is 65% a safe initial estimate? We used customer guidance + sample trace.
- Can Nebula accept int4 quantized outputs for 100% of the pilot cohort? We need to run the eval set to detect rare regressions.
- Investigate legal/regulatory constraints for moving data to dedicated/reserved pools if pursued.

Contact/owners: Maya Chen (product-optimize) — primary author; Ethan Blake (solutions-eng) — implementation lead; Priya Nair (applied-ml) — evals & regression monitoring.

This doc is a working model and is intentionally compact — full spreadsheet with per-route rows, hourly peak simulation, and scenario toggles attached in the linked artifacts (JIRA-OPT-1243 and github PR above).
